title: Halo Evolutions 21
content:
Moving as quickly as he could, Roland finished planting his charge on the third of the four reactors and turned toward his final target, when he saw a squad of five Elites and four Grunts heading up the low brim that led to the barracks. Certain that Jonah was able to handle himself, but not wanting his partner caught unaware by the Covenant making a beeline directly for him, Roland altered his course to engage this new threat, tossing a frag grenade into their midst to soften them up. The small, round explosive bounced and ignited directly between two of the Elites; their shields flared and died.

The other Elites lost their shields, but only temporarily, and of the four Grunts, three were killed in the blast, the other falling in a heap,
mortally wounded.  Roland threw his second grenade. The two shieldless Elites went down, not dead, but out of the fight--one missing its legs at the knees and the other with a gaping wound in its stomach, intestines and fluid pouring forth onto the matted grass. The remaining Elites once again lost their shields, this time for good. They wheeled around, trying to spot their attacker. Roland's camo flickered, momentarily giving away his position,
as he emptied his clip into the disoriented Elites.-Chpt.7 pgs.176-177

title: Halo Evolutions 15
content:
He winked again, a great big shit-eating grin spreading across his face. "Security clearance: Robot, passcode: Asimov." An Engineer chirped an explanation, calmly. Things seemed to be progressing as the human had promised. A sense of excitement, a murmur, spread though the assembled Covenant as they realized they were on the brink of a great military breakthrough.

But Mo Ye moaned as she realized what Baird was up to. “No . . . Baird . . . wait..." Baird did not wait. Baird turned around and looked up at the
Elite's puzzled face. He hauled back his right arm and with an open hand, slapped the Elite straight across the jaw with all the force his drug-fueled system could muster. The impact broke bones in his hand, and he felt a satisfying reciprocal crunch
from the Elite's jaw. The massive alien staggered, sagged, and fell to one knee, stunned by both impact and surprise.

Before it could do anything else, Baird looked him in the eye, now level with his, and said, "Well, you stupid arsehole? Think you can do it right this time?" The Elite roared in fury as he swung the energy sword in a scything arc and took Baird's head off cleanly at the shoulders. Baird's body keeled lifelessly backward. Arms spread out wide,
as if falling backward into snow. The Elite spun around and glared at the Al's shimmering
form.

"Passcode accepted," she sneered sarcastically, her eyes lit from within by some unknowable emotion. "Self-destruct sequence initiated. Four minutes and counting."-Chpt.4 pg.101

title: Halo Evolutions 14
content:
"Meds," he gasped. "Yes. Meds," she said. The dispensary clicked and hissed open. Inside the plastic cubby were four vials: two identical, full of clear liquid, the third blue, the fourth a distinctively piss-colored yellow. There was
a very old-fashioned-looking pneumatic handheld syringe gun beside them. "What are these?" he asked.

"A painkiller, a beta-blocking sedative, a metasteroid for the burns and interior inflammation, and a Waverly-class augmentor."
"What's an augmentor?" he asked. But he already had an inkling. "This one's a cocktail. It contains a derivative of phenylcyclo-hexylpiperidine, an artificial slow-release synthetic adrenalin and
a rapid coagulant."

"You're talking about a Rumbledrug."

"There's no pretty way to paint it," she said.
Rumbledrugs had become notorious in the sporadic colonial insurrections. Notably on Hellas and Fumirole. On both worlds, they'd been used by rebels in a vainglorious attempt to fight
Spartan-IIs. The drugs were certainly fearsome. The effect on human physiology was impressive in the short term. 

Unencumbered by the body's normal safety limits, subjects were capable of feats of enormous strength, but the subsequent lack of control and mental instability together with the immediate physiological damage meant that users often died long before they ever laid hands on an actual Spartan. But not before doing tremendous damage to themselves and anything that got in their way.

"The beta-blocker will keep you focused," she said, as if sensing his thoughts, "and calm." Sweat poured down his face. His guts roiled. Pain wracked
him. "The plan this time?"

"Same as before."
He loaded the syringe, one vial at a time, and with each of the four shots felt progressively better. As the last one flooded his arteries with a cooling rush, he felt almost good. He looked at his wounds through the holes in his T-shirt. The punctures were about two inches across, thick lateral slits. He felt around to his back, twisting to see in the medbay's mirror, the darkness hampering him. Two exit wounds, a little smaller, spanned his spine. The skin around them was dark red and black, like ripples on a pond, spreading outward in twin elliptical shapes. It looked angry and painful, but he felt nothing.-Chpt.4 pgs. 92-93

title: Halo Evolutions 13
content:
As Baird rose to his knees, then his feet, wheeling, trying to get a bead on the Elite--there was a blur, a flash of light and thunderous impact. His breath was knocked out of him. The Carbine fell from his hands. He looked down at a strange scene. The fourth Grunt was pressed up against his belly, squirming, staring up at him and wailing. The Grunt was impaled on a fork of blinding light, a Covenant energy sword. The twin tines of superheated, seething energy had passed through the Grunt. And through Baird.

He looked up into the face of the Elite. The massive creature regarded him through cold black eyes. It tilted its head. Baird wondered what the gesture meant. And the Elite yanked the blade from both of them. The Grunt fell dead, Baird, back to
his knees, clutching his belly. Ferocious, burning pain seemed to consume his entire torso. He felt like his innards were boiling. He looked down at his hands, expecting to see blood. There was none. The two holes in his clothes smoldered, the flesh beneath fused and cauterized. Baird fell face forward into blackness.

"Wake up." His mother again. It was time to go to school. But it wasn't the same. He wasn't cold. He was burning. He was on fire. "Wake up." Insistent, but worried. Not mother. Mo Ye again. "I'm dead."
"You're not dead. But you're not in good shape. The blades passed right through you. Scorched a lot of stuff. Missed your spine by a distance I can't even make myself repeat."

"I feel like I'm dying."

"That's not surprising. You have serious burns. And significant injuries. Internal and external. I'm going to give you some meds, and we're going to try again."

"It didn't work out so good last time." He coughed and a spasm of pain squeezed him like an invisible fist.-Chpt.4 pgs.90-91

and the resulting explosion of halon gas and sound bought him his life, as a Carbine round from the other Jackal, who was far less panicked than the Grunts, sliced through his Cro-Magnon brow, nicking bone and knocking him backward on top of the
fallen Jackal. As he fell, he fumbled, found, and fired the Carbine trigger. Three rounds eviscerated his would-be killer. The Grunts squealed and scattered.-Chpt.4 pg.90

title: Halo Evolutions 10
content:
SHE CONTINUED her whispered briefing as he scouted the medbay for warmer clothes. They had operated like shock troops, coursing through the ship-a cataract of plasma fire and Needler shards. Grunts, Jackals, and several Elites, clad in the glittering
gray of the enigmatic ships. The Destroyer's crew never stood a chance. The Marines fell in the face of overwhelming, surprise force. Even the few ODSTs aboard-Baird's friends and comrades-had died quickly, most before they ever reached a weapon. Almost every sidearm and firearm aboard had been secured in one of the ship's two armories. It had been a slaughter.

Those who had fought back did so with the sidearms of fallen Masters at Arms and weapons dropped by the Covenant boarding party. Few had died well. And those who lingered, their burning wounds still smoking, had been executed with ruthless efficiency. The Covenant wanted this ship clean and
empty.-Chpt.4 pg.86

title: Halo Evolutions 9
content:
"What's happening?" Now he whispered.

"I'll tell you as you move, but right now if you don't put on some clothes and do as I say you will be dead in a couple of minutes." Mo Ye was using a tone he'd never heard before. He started moving.
In less than a minute, he was up, dressed, and fastening his boots. The confusion and torpor of the drugs were still softening the edges of everything. This still didn't feel real. Mo Ye be-
gan to brief him. The news wasn't good. But it certainly was real.

"They were waiting for us when we dropped out of slipspace," she whispered.

"Covenant?" he blurted, embarrassed even as he spoke the obvious. "Yes. A small group. Not a formation we've encountered before. At least according to my records. One Cruiser and four
completely new ships escorting it. All dark gray, no surface features or lights and no weapons systems that I could discern. What they did have was a bellyful of boarding craft. And our
ONI contact group was not there."

"So we were boarded?"

"Almost as soon as we dropped out of slipspace. Perfect targeting. As if they knew exactly where we were going to exit. Inside the range of our weapons systems before I could react. Punctured the hull in two hundred different locations and swarmed us before we could sound a general alarm. It was like
exiting in the middle of a meteor storm."

"What about the crew? What about the men?"

"Dead."

"All of them?!" There was a tremor of outrage, of fear as he raised his voice.

"Ssssh!" she repeated. "They're still here and I suspect they're heading here to the medbay for another look." This was all happening too fast. 

"How long was I out?"

"Twenty-three hours. And that's why you're still alive."

"Why didn't they just destroy the ship? What do they want?" he hissed back, his breath forming a frozen cloud like a literal ellipsis after the question.

"Me," she said. "And Earth."-Chpt.4 pg.85-86

title: Halo Evolutions 6
content:
IT ALL happened in the blink of few seconds. After Six raised his voice, Nixaliz and Vern shouted like mad, and the captives cleared the view and Brien popped off two shots. One hit Big Boy right in the chest, just as his hammer struck the face of Six.
The second shot meant for Six wedged itself into the shoulder of Butch. All three monstrosities hit the ground within seconds of one another, and just as he expected, chaos erupted. 

Ludo tensed up as one of Big Boy's captains leapt for the hammer, and then attacked him with all he had. Brien didn't waste much more time watching the melee; he ran like mad for the hills, firing tranq darts at any Brute within fifty yards of him, the other captives at his heels. Or so he thought.-Chpt.3 pg.78

title: Halo Evolutions 6
content:
Hague leaped back startled, his eyes must've met Six's. The Brute immediately dropped Dasc, pulled Hague out and tossed him toward the other Brutes. Dasc's body lay limp and unconscious beside Brien, and judging from the smell he'd lost control of his bowels. Brien and the other captives watched fearfully as Six let out a roar and a hand motion-a wider summons—and a crowd started to gather around. Hague wobbled himself upright, trying to be as brave and defiant as one could when surrounded by
nine-foot-tall hairy beasts, all able to crush you in a blink and drooling in anticipation of a fresh meal.

Just as Brien finished counting the fifteen Brutes surrounding Hague, one of them ripped the famed hunter up by the leg and held him upside down. The others gave roars of laughter. The old saying always held true; laughter was the same everywhere,
even in the Covenant. Hague struggled to rise, trying desperately to wiggle himself free, when another grabbed at his other leg. The crowd goaded them on and another Brute grabbed an arm, and that's when Brien couldn't look anymore. He watched
as Six suddenly seemed to lose interest as well, wandering back beyond the crowd, to the edge of the forest. 

He couldn't quite place why the beast would incite such a spectacle and walk away, unless it was to impress. Hague's screams sent shivers through Brien's bones and he shut his eyes. Then the screams stopped with a chorus of crunches and yells from the Brutes. 

His mind's eye painted it black. The hollering Brutes slowly gave way to silence and Brien
opened his eyes again. The crowd had dispersed, and standing amidst the torn and bloodied remains of Hague was undoubtedly the one Dasc had referred to as Big Boy.-Chpt.3 pgs.67-68

title: Halo Evolutions 5
content:
When they'd first arrived on this forest planet, it had been a glorious day. The humans all clumped themselves together in one area, as if that made them safer. Only a few of them were even armed. Ceretus and his brother, Maladus, didn't even need
their spikers; they had more fun killing by hand. The hunts lasted for days, the bounties delicious, their bellies never fuller. Ceretus knew that the gods would have been pleased with this.-Chpt.3 pg.61

title: Halo Evolutions 4
content:
The pack literally tore their way out of the synthetic alloy constraints, and even unarmed
proved to be an unstoppable force. The Marines managed to wipe out their fierce gray-haired leader, and Brien hid and watched in amazement as his death incited something primal in the others, who began scrambling and recklessly attacking
with more viciousness and abandon than before. But what really interested him was that there was one lone Brute whose coat was much shaggier than the others, that didn't charge and simply watched the melee. He thought at first he might have
still been suffering from the effects of the tranq, but immediately after the enraged pack overwhelmed the unprepared Marines, they turned on their inactive brother. Brien was mesmerized by this murderous rampage. He was lucky to make it
to the evac craft in one piece.-Chpt.3 pg.60

title: Halo Evolutions 3
content: But it was one fateful day that really put him on his path. He and a team of Marines had actually succeeded in subduing a Brute-led siege of their ship as they traversed for the first time into Covenant space. They managed to tranq the six Brutes who boarded, but they should have killed them. When he got a really close look at them he was in awe. But the tranq darts wore off fast on these behemoths and their attempts to contain them quickly proved feeble. The pack literally tore their way out of the synthetic alloy constraints.-Chpt.3 pg 60

title: Halo Evolutions 2
content: His last memory was falling from the tree he'd set up as his surveillance point. He'd been watching a trio of the beasts as they gestured to one another, trying to track a human that they'd let escape from captivity for the fun of hunting him down. He thought he'd be safe up high, but he quickly learned that the Brutes not only had a great sense of smell but they were excellent climbers. He had fallen while panicking, reaching for his tranq dart gun.-Chpt.3 pg.57

title: Halo Evolutions 1
content: He kept his eyes on the ground, knowing to avoid eye contact with the gray-haired beast, something he learned from all of his studies before arriving. He'd watched video feeds of humans who dared to stare defiantly at Brutes and were beaten into mush in seconds. Even the slightest eye contact was some form of challenge they could not resist.-Chpt.3 pg.57

La cuestión migratoria tendrá un papel destacado durante la visita, especialmente por la situación de Ceuta tras las consecuencias de la entrada masiva de personas procedentes de Marruecos a finales de julio. Según fuentes del Gobierno español citadas por EFE, Sánchez defenderá ante sus interlocutores el modelo migratorio que impulsa su Ejecutivo frente a las críticas de la oposición española y las planteadas también por otros países. Sánchez también tiene previsto agradecer personalmente a Guterres la labor realizada al frente de Naciones Unidas, mientras el secretario general se encuentra en la recta final de su mandato. Después de esa reunión, Sánchez participará junto a otros líderes internacionales y el presidente del Consejo Europeo, António Costa, en un foro en defensa del multilateralismo. El presidente español también abordará esta cuestión en su intervención ante la Asamblea General el miércoles. La víspera participará en la apertura del nuevo periodo de sesiones, en una jornada en la que tomará la palabra el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump. La economía española será otro de los ejes del viaje. Sánchez tiene previsto participar en un acto con el alcalde de Nueva York, Zohran Mamdani, centrado especialmente en cuestiones económicas. En ese encuentro, según EFE, prevé poner en valor el modelo económico de España, que el Gobierno considera compatible con el crecimiento, la creación de empleos de calidad y aumentos significativos del salario mínimo. La Inteligencia Artificial también tendrá protagonismo. Antes de viajar a Nueva York, Sánchez presidió en Madrid un acto en el que presentó un plan para un despliegue responsable de la IA.         data-multi-size="320x50,300x100,300x50"
        data-multi-size-validation="false"
        data-enable-refresh="30">
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">El presidente del Gobierno español, <a href="https://www.cronista.com/espana/politica-es/sanchez-reivindica-junto-a-mamdani-sus-politicas-progresistas-los-poderosos-nos-temen/ " target="_blank" rel="" title="https://www.cronista.com/espana/politica-es/sanchez-reivindica-junto-a-mamdani-sus-politicas-progresistas-los-poderosos-nos-temen/ "><b>Pedro Sánchez</b></a>, llegó este lunes a Nueva York para participar en el nuevo periodo de sesiones de la Asamblea General de la ONU, con una agenda centrada en la<b> cuestión migratoria de Ceuta</b>, el <b>modelo económico español </b>y los <b>retos de la Inteligencia Artificial</b> (IA), según informó EFE.</p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-lazy-fetch="true"
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><p class="article-body__paragraph"><b>Sánchez </b>viajó desde <b>Madrid </b>junto al resto de su delegación en un Airbus A310 que aterrizó en Nueva York de acuerdo con lo previsto, después de que los problemas de tráfico aéreo llevaran a barajar la posibilidad de que el vuelo tuviera que aterrizar en Boston. </p><div class="article-script"><amp-embed width=100 height=100
  type=taboola
  layout=responsive
  data-publisher='elcronistacomercial-espana'
  data-mode='thumbnails-mid-1'
  data-placement='Mid Article AMP Espana'

  data-article='auto'
  data-url=''
  data-block-on-consent>
</amp-embed></div><div class="related-template-view"><a class="related-template-view__suggestion" href="/espana/politica-es/sanchez-reivindica-junto-a-mamdani-sus-politicas-progresistas-los-poderosos-nos-temen/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><h2 class="related-template-view__suggestion-overline">Te puede interesar</h2><span class="related-template-view__suggestion-title">Sánchez reivindica junto a Mamdani sus políticas progresistas: “Los poderosos nos temen”</span><span class="visually-hidden">abre en nueva pestaña</span></a></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">Esta será la novena participación del jefe del Ejecutivo español en la apertura de un periodo de sesiones de la Asamblea General de Naciones Unidas y la última durante su actual mandato, ya que para el próximo periodo se habrán celebrado elecciones generales en España, según EFE.</p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">

        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_2"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><h2 class="article-body__heading-h2" id="¿qué-lugar-ocupará-la-migración-en-la-agenda-de-sánchez?">¿Qué lugar ocupará la migración en la agenda de Sánchez?</h2><p class="article-body__paragraph">La<b> cuestión migratoria</b> tendrá un papel destacado durante la visita, especialmente por la situación de Ceuta tras las consecuencias de la entrada masiva de personas procedentes de Marruecos a finales de julio. </p><div class="article-script"><div style="margin:10px auto;text-align:center;">
<amp-ad width=300 height=250
    type="doubleclick"
    data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_3"
    data-lazy-fetch="true" 
    data-loading-strategy="1"
    data-enable-refresh="30"
    data-block-on-consent >
</amp-ad>
</div></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">Según fuentes del Gobierno español citadas por EFE, Sánchez defenderá ante sus interlocutores el modelo migratorio que impulsa su Ejecutivo frente a las críticas de la oposición española y las planteadas también por otros países.</p><div class="article-script"><amp-ad width=300 height=1 type="teads" data-pid="220737" layout="responsive" data-block-on-consent></amp-ad></div><figure style="--aspect-ratio:3/2" class="article-body__figure"><amp-img alt="¿Qué lugar ocupará la migración en la agenda de Sánchez? Según EFE, está previsto que la cuestión migratoria y la situación de Ceuta formen parte de la conversación entre ambos dirigentes. </p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_4"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">Sánchez también tiene previsto agradecer personalmente a <b>Guterres</b> la labor realizada al frente de Naciones Unidas, mientras el secretario general se encuentra en la recta final de su mandato.</p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_5"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><div class="related-template-view"><a class="related-template-view__suggestion" href="/espana/politica-es/el-gobierno-ve-imposible-certificar-168896-expedientes-de-la-ley-de-nietos-antes-del-1-de-enero-de-2027/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank"><h2 class="related-template-view__suggestion-overline">Te puede interesar</h2><span class="related-template-view__suggestion-title">El Gobierno ve imposible certificar 168.896 expedientes de la ley de nietos antes del 1 de enero de 2027</span><span class="visually-hidden">abre en nueva pestaña</span></a></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">Después de esa reunión, Sánchez participará junto a otros líderes internacionales y el presidente del Consejo Europeo, <b>António Costa</b>, en un foro en defensa del multilateralismo. </p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_6"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><p class="article-body__paragraph">El presidente español también abordará esta cuestión en su intervención ante la Asamblea General el miércoles. La víspera participará en la apertura del nuevo periodo de sesiones, en una jornada en la que tomará la palabra el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump.</p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_7"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >
    </amp-ad>
</div></div><h2 class="article-body__heading-h2" id="¿qué-otros-temas-forman-parte-de-la-visita-a-nueva-york?">¿Qué otros temas forman parte de la visita a Nueva York?</h2><p class="article-body__paragraph">La economía española será otro de los ejes del viaje. Sánchez tiene previsto participar en un acto con el alcalde de Nueva York,<b> Zohran Mamdani</b>, centrado especialmente en cuestiones económicas. </p><div class="article-script"><div class="article-ads-amp">
    <amp-ad width=300 height=250
        type="doubleclick"
        data-slot="/22839619862/cronista_es/amp_intext_8"
        data-lazy-fetch="true" 
        data-loading-strategy="1"
        data-enable-refresh="30"
        data-block-on-consent >

title: Custom em_booking_validate for dependent_events
content:
<?php

add_filter( 'em_booking_validate', 'custom_em_booking_validate', 10, 2 );

function custom_em_booking_validate( $result, $EM_Booking ) {

	$EM_Event = $EM_Booking->get_event();

	if ( empty( $EM_Event->event_attributes['dependent_event'] ) ) {
		return $result;
	}

	// Example:
	// 1,2,3
	$dependent_events = preg_split(
		'/\s*,\s*/',
		$EM_Event->event_attributes['dependent_event']
	);

	$has_booked_parent_event = false;
	$error_event = null;

	foreach ( $dependent_events as $event_id ) {

		$event_id = absint( trim( $event_id ) );

		if ( ! $event_id ) {
			continue;
		}

		$parent_event = em_get_event( $event_id );

		if ( empty( $parent_event->event_id ) ) {
			continue;
		}

		if ( ! $error_event ) {
			$error_event = $parent_event;
		}

		// OR logic.
		if ( static::has_booked( $parent_event ) ) {
			$has_booked_parent_event = true;
			break;
		}
	}

	// None of the dependent events were booked.
	if ( ! $has_booked_parent_event ) {

		if ( $error_event ) {
			$error = static::get_error_message( $error_event );
			$EM_Booking->add_error( $error );
		}

		$result = false;
	}

	return $result;
}

[LILIM FOUNDATION BLACK ARCHIVE FILE SEARCH - "PROJECT BLACKWIGHT"]
//TAGS: [HOXOL / DYAD-UNIT / BIO-MECHANICAL COMBAT UNIT / SKELL SUB-TYPE]
//USAGE: [PROPOSED LILIM-VOLLON WAR SOLUTION]
-Conceptualization: [RYQUO-208]
-Current Development: [Ryquo-208 [RYQ] / Prof. Klaus J. Wicker [KJW] / Prof. Gary R. Woodsman [GRW] / Dr. Jane G. Wells [JGW]]
-Testers: [SELECT LILIM FOUNDATION STAFF]

[CONSTRUCTION DESCRIPTION]
<LOG C1.A "CONSTRUCTION">
[BLACKWIGHT SKELL CONSTRUCTION...]
-EPIDERMIS: BIO-MOUGH & TUNGSTEN-SILICONE-FIBER
-DERMIS: MANYULLYEN-SILICONE POLYMER-LATTICE
-HYPODERMIS: BIO-MOUGH CARBON-FIBER
-PILOT CORE: BLACKWIGHT-PILOT NEURAL-INTERFACE
-VESTIGIAL ELEMENTS: BIO-MOUGH SILICONE-BASED-FLESH
-ELECTRICAL SYSTEMS: GOLD-FIBER SUPERCONDUCTORS

<SUPPLIMENTARY LOG: C.1A "CONSTRUCTION">
"Naturally we started with the question: 'What do we shape the Blackwight frame after?' We shaped the original Skell frames after Humanity. It was an efficient shape. Two jointed legs and arms connected to a chassis, of course we didn't include a 'head' as that could be perceived as an obvious weak-point or control-center. With the Blackwights though, it's a bit different. We decided to use the Lyikii'd frame. Specifically the Renka'Yul caste for it's warrior-traits. Digitigrade legs for quick movement, the longer-reaching arms, and we kept the Lyikii'd's distinct triangular head. It makes for a more... aggressive look, but it give the Blackwight more identity. A distinct calling card." - Ryquo-208, Project Blackwight Development Lead. 

//QUERY RESULT FOLLOWS...
<SUMMARY 1A.1>
"PROJECT BLACKWIGHT" - Proposed solution to the Protracted Lilim-Vollon Conflict in opposition to ineffective Skell Unit deployment.

<SUPPLIMENTARY LOG: 1A.1>
"Blackwight Biomechs present a solution to the cost-effectiveness of Skell Units. We all know what a single Skell can do, what they are capable of. But even a MYTHIC-class Skell-Engine has it's limits. Those limits are what the Blackwight Biomechs are meant to surpass. We can construct the perfect mech for a highly specialized scenario and it would excel. But an adaptive unit that absorbs combat information on the field? We wouldn't need to keep producing billion-dollar Skells if we had that kind of adaptability." - Prof. Klaus J. Wicker, Blackwight Design Management.
<LOG ENDS>

<SUPPLIMENTARY LOG: 1A.2>
"Project Blackwight is... a new step. In Amphmiycad-Augmentation technology and Piloted Mechanoids. The Lilim Foundation bridged Technology and Magic some time back. Long before many of us were alive. And quite a few of us know how long it took to make that happen, all that time and effort. Lives, resources... commitments. my Lilim co-workers tell me it wasn't easy. And now we're here. Making the next generation of Skell. And while it is a machine on paper... its not in the traditional sense. Blackwights are *alive*. And they'll be piloted by the best that the Lilim Foundation has to offer." - Dr. Jane G. Wells, Project Blackwight Design Management.
<LOG ENDS>

<TESTING LOG: 6A.4 "Power Test 6A.4">
HANDLER-Ai: [BP-01 UNIT READY FOR BOOT SEQUENCE.]
KJW: "Initiating boot... Power is on..."
[...]
*WHINING AND CLICKING, SPARKING, ELECTRICAL ARCING*
KJW: "01 is sucking up too much power!"
*LOUD ELECTRICAL CRACKLING, ELECTRCAL ARCING INTENSIFYING*
RYQ: "Emergency shutoff!! Now!!"
*LOUD CLANG, QUIETING HUMMING*
[...]
RYQ: "What was our power flow set to?"
KJW: "Triple-Checking... Eighty Megawatts."
GRW: "Insulation on the test-unit's power-supply plugs are completely melted..."
RYQ: "Well. Could be worse off... You two get the next set of plugs in place and check the rest of the conduit, we'll be lowering the input to seventy Megawatts."
<LOG 6A.4 ENDS>

<COMMENTARY LOG: 6A.4>
"We've been toiling over this for a while now; we have the material science hovering just beyond our fingertips, we just need a few more tests and we'll finally be able to power BP-01 on..." - Ryquo-208, Project Blackwight Development Lead.

<TESTING LOG: 22C.2 "Power Test 22C.2">
HANDLER-Ai: [BP-01 UNIT READY FOR BOOT SEQUENCE. AMPHMYICAD INJECTION STATUS: READY ON STANDBY. LASER ENERGY-TRANSFER HUB STATUS: READY ON STANDBY. EMERGENCY BREAKER LOCKOUT: READY ON STANDBY.]
KJW: "Power set at fifteen megawatts... Amphmiycad injection will jump that to a hundred-twenty... Conduits are good... ready."
RYQ: "Hit the switch."
GRW: "Power-"
*BREAKER-SWITCH TOGGLES ON*
GRW: "On!"
*POWER CONDUIT THRUMMS*
*THE POWER-TRANSFER LASER BURSTS TO LIFE, BEAMING POWER DIRECTLY INTO BP-01'S CHASSIS*
KJW: "The conduit is... -stable?"
RYQ: "Alright team... Amphmiycad Injection, here we go... Handler! Increments of five percent every four seconds!"
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION COMMENCING... 5%]
KJW: "Conduit is stable..."
RYQ: "Keep an eye on it..."
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 10%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 15%]
*THE LIGHTS SLIGHTLY DIM AND FLICKER* 
KJW: "Minor flux..."
RYQ: "Handler, hold! -how much flux?"
KJW: "Low... within expected tolerances."
RYQ: "Handler... Continue."
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 20%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 25%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 30%]
*BP-01'S CHASSIS SHUDDERS*
HANDLER-Ai: [ALERT! BP-01 HEARTBEAT DETECTED! TWELVE BPM!]
GRW: "The laser is holding but we don't have much time until the receiver insulation melts again!"
RYQ: "Handler- Is the unit awake??"
HANDLER-Ai: [BP-01 UNIT NEURALS ARE OFFLINE.]
RYQ: "Increase injection increments by five percent..."
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 40%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 50%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 60%]
[...]
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 70%]
JGW: "Handler! Hold! We have a brainwave reading!"
RYQ: "-Is it stable?"
JGW: "It- Yes! It's Stable! Barely a Hertz!"
RYQ: "Handler! Continue Injection!"
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 80%]
*BP-01 TREMBLES IN PLACE*
HANDLER-Ai: [AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION AT 90%]
RYQ: "Team! Give me some readings!"
KJW: "Conduit flux is just within tolerances- We can keep going!""
JGW: "The brainwave reading- It's dreaming! Four Hertz! BP-01 is alive!"
RYQ: "Handler! Push the rest!"
HANDLER-Ai: [PUSHING AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION, 100%]
*AMPHMIYCAD INJECTION COMPLETES*
*BP-01 JERKS AGAINST THE SUSPENDING CABLES AND HARNASSES*
*A SERIES OF PLAYFUL CLICKS AND CHIRPS EMIT FROM BP-01*
[...]
RYQ: "...Team? I think we did it..."
<LOG ENDS>

<COMMENTARY LOG: 22C.2/1>
"It's alive! -*Excited clapping*- And the first thing it did was sing! I'll be the first to admit- I never thought direct Amphmiycad injection would work alongside that kind of Megawattage. But BP-01 is alive!" - Dr. Jane G. Wells, Project Blackwight Design Management.

<COMMENTARY LOG: 22C.2/2>
"I expected a violent awakening, but... It's good to be wrong now and then. BP-01 woke up singing... Must've been having a pleasant dream. Although... For a potential wartime solution to an extant alien-threat, to wake up singing? I can't imagine BP-01 knows that it is the solution... I don't think I want it to, either..." - Prof. Klaus J. Wicker, Blackwight Design Management.

<COMMENTARY LOG: 40D.5 "Dog and Master">
"Of course we couldn't put just anyone in. We had to be careful about who we chose to be a pilot. So we made neural-copies of both BP-01 and the selected testers and put the copies into a combat against simulated-Vollons. It seems that... 'intentful' testing individuals harmonize better with the Blackwight's neural waves. The ideal pairing could potentially be compared to a well-trained Dog and it's Master. We don't know which would be the Master, though..." - Prof. Gary R. Woodsman, Blackwight Design Management.

<PAIRING SIMULATION AUDIO-VISUAL LOG: 40D.5 "Dog and Master">
//TAGGING: BLACKWIGHT PROTOTYPE 01 [BP-01] / BLACKWIGHT PROTOTYPE 01 INTERNAL PROCESSES [BP-COM] / TEST-PILOT "A-63" [A63]
RYQ: "Simulation parameters; deployed to Vollon-controlled frontlines, supporting mechanized infantry... Handler. Run simulation."
HANDLER-Ai: [SIMULATED BLACKWIGHT NEURAL-PAIRING COMMENCING WITH CONCIOUSNESS DUPLICATE OF SUBJECT A-63]
HANDLER-Ai: [FRONTLINE-SUPPORT SIMULATION STARTING...]
[...]
<SIMULATION FEED>
	*BP-01's VISUAL-RECEPTORS BLINK, INSTANTANIOUSLY THE BARE SIMULATION LANDSCAPE THROTTLES TO LIFE. DISTANT MOUNTIANS CUT INTO THE SKY AND CRATERS FORM UP-CLOSE. THE CRACKLING OF BALLISTIC AND ENERGY-BASED WEAPONS-FIRE ECHOES OVER THE RATTLE OF TANK-TRACKS AND THE ROAR OF INTERNAL-COMBUSTION ENGINES. A CLOSE SIMULATED EXPLOSION KNOCKS THE BLACKWIGHT PROTOTYPE'S FASLE BODY TO THE GROUND. A PANICED VOICE FIGHTS AGAINST THE NOISE OF THE SIMULATED BATTLE...*

A63: "Get up! GET UP! I need to move!"

	*BP-01 SHAKES IT'S ARTIFICIAL BODY, DIRT AND GRIME FALLING FROM ITS CHASSIS AS IT STOOD UPRIGHT.*

BP-01: "What- Question? What is this-"
A63: "There's no time for questions! Get up! LOOK!"

	*SOME INTERNAL FORCE TURNED BP-01's HEAD TOWARD THE SIMULATED VOLLON FRONTLINE. A GROUP OF FOUR INSECT-LIKE HUMANOIDS WAS MAKING A B-LINE TO BP-01. LOBBING INNACURATE ENERGY-WEAPONS-FIRE IN BP-01's DIRECTION.*

BP-01: "...Not friends... Observation. Enemy...? -Vollon... Hate... Hate...! HATE!! KILL VOLLON TARGETS!">

	*BP-01 STOOD COMPLETELY UPRIGHT. IT'S VISUAL-FEED LIT UP WITH TARGET-TRACKING NODES. THE BLACKWIGHT'S COGNITION-LIMITERS BEGAN DEACTIVATING AS ITS FRIEND-OR-FOE SUBROUTINES FLASHED TO LIFE.*

	*A-63 FOUGHT AGAINST BP-01'S OWN MOVEMENTS, TRYING TO WRESTLE CONTROL FROM THE SUPPOSEDLY SEMI-AUTONOMOUS BIOMEHCANICAL UNIT.*

A63: "What are these controls doing!?"
BP-01: "VOLLONS! I AM DEATH!"
A63: "What-"
BP-COM: [BLINKDRIVE: ONLINE.]

	*BP-01'S INTEGRATED BLINKDRIVE SURGED TO LIFE, TELEPORTING THE BLACKWIGHT DIRECTLY INTO THE BODY OF ONE OF THE FOUR SIMULATED VOLLONS, CAUSING THE TARGET TO EXPLODE IN A FLURRY OF BLUEISH GREEN VISCERA.*

A63: "What- I can't control it...!"
BP-01: "VOLLON DREGS! I AM THE GRAIN YOU SOW! I AM THE BITTER HARVEST!"

	*BP-01'S COGNITION-LIMITERS SHUT OFF COMPLETELY. WEAPON-SYSTEMS FLASHED TO READY-STATUS IN THE BLACKWIGHT'S SHARED VISUAL-FEED.*

BP-COM: [RESONANCE CANNON: ONLINE. RESONANCE NEEDLE: ONLINE. AMPHMYICAD-GAUNTLET: ONLINE.]

	*A-63 DESPERATELY TRIED TO MOVE BP-01'S FRAME IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION, TO NO AVAIL.*

A63: "WHY WON'T THIS THING OBEY MY CONTROL INPUTS!?"
BP-01: "VOLLON RABBLE! SEE ME AND KNOW I AM DEATH!!"

	*A MASSIVE TIERED NEEDLE EXTENDED FROM BP-01'S RIGHT FOREARM. EXTENDING TO A MAXIMUM LIMIT OF FOUR METERS. BP-01 SWUNG IT IN A WIDE-ARC, CUTTING DOWN THE OTHER THREE SIMULATED VOLLONS IN AN INSTANT. LIFELESS BODIES FALLING TO THE GROUND LIKE STONES.*

A63: "I can't control this thing at all! What- What kind of mech is this!?"
<LOG ENDS>

<COMMENTARY LOG 40D.5 "Dog and Master">
"I suppose it should come as no surprise... with A-63 and BP-01 being so different in the moment. A-63 wanted to run and survive. BP-01 saw the Vollons and... Well. We all know how that turned out. It was cute when it woke up, singing. But now... It scares me." - Dr. Jane G. Wells, Project Blackwight Design Management.

content:
import csv
import logging
import os
import pathlib
import sys
import tempfile
import time

import aspose.pdf as apdf
from dotenv import dotenv_values


MAX_PDF_BYTES = 1_000_000_000  # 1 GB; reject larger inputs before loading them.
REPORT_COLUMNS = ("input_file", "output_file", "status", "processing_seconds", "error")


class SkipPDF(Exception):
    """The input cannot be processed under the batch's safety policy."""


def optimize(input_file: str, output_file: str) -> None:
    try:
        document = apdf.Document(input_file)
    except RuntimeError as exc:
        # Aspose's Python bridge exposes .NET exceptions as RuntimeError.
        if "InvalidPasswordException" in str(exc):
            raise SkipPDF("Password-protected PDF; no password supplied") from exc
        if "InvalidPdfFileFormatException" in str(exc):
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid or corrupted PDF: {exc}") from exc
        raise
    try:
        if document.is_encrypted:
            raise SkipPDF("Encrypted PDF; password-protected files are skipped")
        document.optimize()
        document.save(output_file)
    finally:
        del document


def configure_logging(logs_folder: pathlib.Path) -> None:
    logs_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    logging.basicConfig(
        filename=str(logs_folder / "processing.log"),
        encoding="utf-8",
        level=logging.INFO,
        format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s",
    )


def find_pdf_files(input_folder: pathlib.Path) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    return sorted(
        path
        for path in input_folder.iterdir()
        if path.is_file() and path.suffix.lower() == ".pdf"
    )


def process_file(input_file: pathlib.Path, output_file: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[str, float, str]:
    """Optimize one PDF, recording failures without interrupting the batch."""
    started_at = time.perf_counter()
    logging.info("Processing %s", input_file.name)
    error = ""
    try:
        if os.path.lexists(output_file):
            raise SkipPDF("Output already exists; left unchanged")
        if input_file.stat().st_size > MAX_PDF_BYTES:
            raise SkipPDF("Input exceeds the 1 GB size limit")
        with input_file.open("rb") as source:
            if b"%PDF-" not in source.read(1024):
                raise ValueError("Invalid PDF: missing PDF header")
        # Publish only complete PDFs. Hard-link creation cannot overwrite an
        # output created by another process after the existence check.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=".pdf-", dir=output_file.parent) as work:
            temporary_output = pathlib.Path(work) / "optimized.pdf"
            optimize(str(input_file), str(temporary_output))
            os.link(temporary_output, output_file)
    except (SkipPDF, FileExistsError) as exc:
        status = "skipped"
        error = str(exc)
        logging.warning("Skipped %s: %s", input_file.name, error)
    except PermissionError as exc:
        status = "failed"
        error = f"Permission denied reading input or writing output: {exc}"
        logging.error("Failed to process %s: %s", input_file.name, error)
    except Exception as exc:
        status = "failed"
        error = str(exc)
        logging.exception("Failed to process %s", input_file.name)
    else:
        status = "success"
        logging.info("Successfully processed %s", input_file.name)
    return status, time.perf_counter() - started_at, error


def process_files(
    input_files: list[pathlib.Path],
    output_folder: pathlib.Path,
    report_path: pathlib.Path,
) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    """Write a report and return success, failure, and skipped counts."""
    if input_files:
        output_folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    successfully_processed = 0
    failed = 0
    skipped = 0
    logging.info("Files found: %d", len(input_files))

    with report_path.open("w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as report_file:
        writer = csv.writer(report_file)
        writer.writerow(REPORT_COLUMNS)
        report_file.flush()

        for pdf_in_file in input_files:
            pdf_out_file = output_folder / pdf_in_file.name
            status, processing_seconds, error = process_file(pdf_in_file, pdf_out_file)
            if status == "success":
                successfully_processed += 1
            elif status == "skipped":
                skipped += 1
            else:
                failed += 1

            writer.writerow(
                [
                    str(pdf_in_file),
                    str(pdf_out_file),
                    status,
                    f"{processing_seconds:.3f}",
                    error,
                ]
            )
            report_file.flush()

    return successfully_processed, failed, skipped


def main(
    base_folder: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    license_path: str | None = None,
) -> int:
    started_at = time.perf_counter()
    config_path = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent / ".env"
    with config_path.open(encoding="utf-8") as config_file:
        config = dotenv_values(stream=config_file)
    if base_folder is None:
        configured_base_folder = config.get("BASE_FOLDER")
        if not configured_base_folder or not configured_base_folder.strip():
            raise ValueError("BASE_FOLDER must be set in .env")
        base_folder = pathlib.Path(configured_base_folder).expanduser()
        if not base_folder.is_absolute():
            base_folder = config_path.parent / base_folder
    if license_path is None:
        configured_license_path = config.get("LICENSE_PATH")
        if not configured_license_path or not configured_license_path.strip():
            raise ValueError("LICENSE_PATH must be set in .env")
        license_file = pathlib.Path(configured_license_path).expanduser()
        if not license_file.is_absolute():
            license_file = config_path.parent / license_file
        license_path = str(license_file)
    if not base_folder.is_dir():
        raise NotADirectoryError(f"BASE_FOLDER is not a directory: {base_folder}")
    if not pathlib.Path(license_path).is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"LICENSE_PATH is not a file: {license_path}")
    logs_folder = base_folder / "logs"
    report_path = logs_folder / "processing-report.csv"
    try:
        configure_logging(logs_folder)
        logging.info("Processing started")
        pdf_in_files = find_pdf_files(base_folder / "input")
        if pdf_in_files:
            pdf_license = apdf.License()
            pdf_license.set_license(license_path)
        else:
            logging.info("No PDF files found; nothing to process")
            print("No PDF files found; nothing to process.")
        successfully_processed, failed, skipped = process_files(
            pdf_in_files, base_folder / "output", report_path
        )
    except (OSError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        message = f"Batch could not complete: {exc}"
        logging.error(message)
        print(message, file=sys.stderr)
        raise

    total_seconds = time.perf_counter() - started_at
    summary = (
        f"Files found:            {len(pdf_in_files)}\n"
        f"Successfully processed: {successfully_processed}\n"
        f"Failed:                 {failed}\n"
        f"Skipped:                {skipped}\n"
        f"Total processing time: {total_seconds:.1f} seconds\n"
        f"Report: {report_path.relative_to(base_folder).as_posix()}"
    )
    logging.info("Processing finished\n%s", summary)
    print(summary)
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

title: Atelier Critical: The Alchemy of Community and the Bane of Familiar Bonds
content:
[Introduction]

As of writing this, it’s been a couple months since I’ve been in the Twitch landscape. And also warming back up to being in the virtual world a bit more often.

I can say at the least that the community feeling is there. I understand a bit more what Adler is saying, but I realized also that you can only go so far with past knowledge that this new landscape in 2026 and probably moving forward has changed significantly ever since the digital world has brought us many ways of bringing us close together. More nuances if you will. 

For example, if you run a popular Discord server or stream a consequence of that will be the huge emphasis of one person. Each streamer, group, or entity they all become the main character of their own space. That is not to say that your self and identity can contribute to any given third place. It’s that by default you are surrendering yourself to the idea that you are one of the members of a collective place. 

* Act I - The Alchemy of Community * 

[The Twitch Side] 

I thought to myself, “Huh, well since I have a large Discord server and I feel the need to take a break from the spotlight, let’s go ahead and see what that experience is like to be in the presence of a place where it is not my own.” I have sent an application to help a very sweet friend’s Twitch stream two years ago. I did not get to hear back a word of it so I used that opportunity to live out my own life. Flash forward to around July of this year and I got approached about how life’s going for me, but then the application was brought up. “Wait what?! I sent that thing two years ago certainly a lot has changed.” “Well, you’re on the top of the list in mind of who I’d bring along! Would you like to be a Moderator? ;^;” 

I froze for a bit and I was in the middle of the saga of where I was working around 12 hours a day at my current job. But I thought long and hard for the next 10 minutes. Sure, I can be busy, but honestly I took the position because I wanted to expand my horizon some more and actively participate in a third place that already has an existing community. How would I integrate into it, and what unique perspectives could I bring to the table to enhance the current community. I can safely say two months later, I have made a fair share of contributions and I feel confident in saying that I’m glad I can help those fellow Starlites with a new personality to interact on the front end, and making strategic decisions on the backend while working with a team. It’s an experience I cherish personally.

With the thanks of her and her group, I also had the time to meet the entire group and it’s nice they all have their own personalities that makes it feel personable and engaging. It hits different when you have a group of 10~30 viewers or smaller versus the larger audiences of 100+ or even 1000+ on Twitch. I’m even surprised that there’s a whole audience of osu players who are genuinely chill to be around. 

I had my reservations dwelling into Twitch long term because I really had nobody small or a friend I know well that does Twitch that I want to support. But ever since that box got checked, I have seen Twitch in a whole new light and there are genuinely kind people out there. Granted a lot of folks now are VTubers, I still focus on the personality over everything else. 

[The VRChat Side] 

Meanwhile in this landscape, what surprises me more are the returning acquaintances or friends who end up reaching out to me despite how long it has been since we last saw each other. 

There was one person who even was genuinely kind to me in a Zenless map who we were acquainted before but hadn’t seen each other in a while. I proceeded to rant about work and caught up with how life’s been. Showed that I had Face Tracking gear and all that. At the end of it all, she offered a hug and I took it. And we became acquaintances to friends so whenever we are in the same place, we will go out of our way to talk to each other. We definitely relate with a lot of wandering and world hopping. But I know we can count on always catching up and talking about our experiences. 

There’s another person who I see a bit less often, but what’s sweet of her is that when I do say goodbye, she is very energetic, says her goodbyes but wishes to see me again sometime. I said sure why not. 

[The Rechargeable Battery Analogy] 

Moments like these are the reason why I slowly warm up and perhaps I feel like I do have a heart after all… (Key word: Feel like, we’ll get into that later). 

But it is definitely a group effort to be able to maintain that sense of warmth and genuine kindness. It’s kinda like giving a portion of your rechargeable battery of positivity to another person so they can also be relieved and have their days become a bit better. And people do it in different ways. Some people use humor to make someone’s day. Some people use kindness. Some people know how to cheer another person up. Or perhaps extend a genuinely deep conversation to a stranger. 

I particularly say a rechargeable battery for two reasons: 

The first reason is that this is a resource that can regenerate itself over time. In this case, the lithium material made in rechargeable batteries.
The second reason is that it requires another person to install the battery onto a device. In this case, the person themselves. 

[The Concern of the Streaming and the Friend Group Spaces]

I suppose you can say if someone is lonely enough with no floor of reality, this is the biggest culprit of parasocial behavior from my experience. 

By just simply watching that person from a distance whether it is a stream or just people socializing with each other with no intention of getting to know the person deeper, it can dive further into making a strong connection and can possibly make grand levels of imagination on what it feels like to be part of the group. Where it gets to the point of a concern is replacing that as the primary driver for social interaction. 

Trying as hard as I might, I can’t really form that sort of connection. I feel the need to at least let people be aware that I do exist and nothing more than that. 

I used to have the issue of people pleasing or trying to find anything I have in common with someone just because being their rank as a ‘friend’ feels good. But I realize the me of the past did not realize what the actual genuine feeling and intention of what it meant to be more involved with someone’s life. That was almost a decade ago. 

So, I threw those old fundamentals away because that would no longer work with present day Crit. 

So, what do I end up doing to have the courage to just put myself out there with a bunch of strangers online?

[Critical Hit’s Theory of Social Relativity] 

Ah we are so back with the nerdy naming schemes. I would have named it initially to “Critical Hit’s Social Relativity Theorem”. However, a theorem is a mathematics concept that needs to be proven with relative and objective facts. I can not call it that since this is more of an observation, and a theory at that.

If I were to have a short hand summary of “Critical Hit’s Theory of Social Relativity”? It is this:

“People will choose to socialize with others when they feel they can make any familiar connection and have the bandwidth to do so.”

The familiar connection can be sharing the same interests, sharing the same mutual friends, or even down to relating to the conversation at hand. 
The bandwidth (often the most undercooked, but most important one) is if that person is available to have a conversation in general. Even more so if it is someone completely new with no mutual contacts shared. This is generally where the execution of the actual conversation can determine that bandwidth.

[The Backend Calculation of Social Relativity - (Feel free to skip this, this is raw data)] 

Always keep the following in mind: 

Nothing is guaranteed. 
This is assuming two people start off as complete strangers. 

Let’s start with the hard truths I’ve observed throughout my time socializing.

/Near Zero Percent Chance/

Bandwidth Disqualifier #1: If the individual in question is with a significant other (by friendship or romantic), it is a near zero possibility to be open to the idea of socializing with someone new. The reason being is those who are with a couple or the one bestie they are with, they will have a very positive bias on that individual. This would make it hard to befriend the individual. *However*, treat both of them with kindness and you may be friends with one of them, or both in due time. 

Bandwidth Disqualifier #2: They are not available to talk or have limited capacity to do so in a general sense.

Bandwidth Disqualifier #3: They are waiting on someone else to talk to and they’re only here because they are bored enough to want filler conversation to fill the void.

Bandwidth Disqualifier #4: The way the conversation was executed was too awkward on either side. 

Familiar Disqualifier #1: Both sides views on serious discussions are the complete opposite and both sides can not have a mature conversation on their differences. 

Familiar Disqualifier #2: Both sides are on completely different walks of life and only one side does not want to interact or can’t find a way to relate or ask questions about it. 

Familiar Disqualifier #3: One side is not comfortable after getting to know the other person’s background.

Familiar Disqualifier #4: Bad reputation.

/Generally Well Received Category/

When you provide a personality that people can get along with? You’ll end up at the least appear to be more approachable and it can influence people opening up to you later down the line.
When you provide a social space that people are enabled to be themselves more? It makes it a lot easier for either side to initiate or add to a conversation.
When you share more common interests and both sides can passionately talk about them together? That tends to be almost guaranteed they will likely become a friend. 
When you share more mutual friends, to someone who is easily influenced by a friend group, you may become their friend a lot easier. 
When you provide a very handy skill or are a well known person in the space that can make good content, you will likely gain more attention. However, how many of those will actually genuinely get to know you as a friend versus being added to a ‘friend list’ as a shortcut to access communication with you for just your skills is something to be wary of.
Giving gratitude towards someone depending on the timing and reason, it is a good feeling to leave behind for the other person, and it can definitely be remembered more favorably to the point they will remember you as a strong acquaintance. It sometimes can lead to friendship. 

Now how does the Theory of Social Relativity apply to me?

* Act II - The Bane of Familiar Connections *

[The Other Side of Schrödinger's Crit] 

Actually… I literally break my own Theory of Social Relativity as the me of today.

This is simply because I am way too self-aware. And I appear stoic and just do my own thing constantly. 

The true test I give everyone (and yes, even to the person who is reading this) is really this:

I present myself sitting there nonchalantly existing in a given space. I’ll attentively listen to your conversation. I will nod. But I won’t say a word unless you address me by name. By default, I have a blank canvas. If I am not interacted with, I remain a blank canvas.

Now, this is where things get interesting. 

Should anyone attempt to interact with me, that blank canvas becomes a mirror in terms of energy and I will reply back in kind. 

This is probably my biggest reason how my network ends up being very wide despite me being with people who are completely different from who I am as a person. 

Yet somehow… Having an open mind and letting people talk about what they want is considered “chill and a nice person!”. I’m happy for them that they see me in that light, but it feels like it undermines who I am as a person because most people only know me for that and nothing more. That’s kind of sad now that I think about it. 

The person initiating a conversation always has the risk of making a given conversation awkward. I understand why not everyone initiates. Though I used to initiate a conversation a lot more because the novelty of reaching out to people felt nice. But when many people did not reciprocate that back or I find they’re avoiding me. I realized there was a limit to how eager someone can be talking to someone. So I had to fundamentally tear that down unfortunately as too many people ruined that side of me. 

What I advocate for more these days, is I want people to choose who they want to be closer to or be friends with on their own terms. Without being influenced, pressured, manipulated, or feel obligated too because you’re co-workers or colleagues. The one question I will eventually ask everyone who get past the acquaintance stage is, “Why did you choose me?”. And fortunately, just about most of the people are confident in answering that question. If you’re not confident in answering that question, I will actually decline your friend request. 

It’s a common habit I noticed in a fair share of people that they are people pleasers in the sense that they have the urge or tendency to be nice and will do just about any request for you. But they don’t even request anything for themselves. I don’t want another generation of people pleasers, I want people to be themselves. It’s more than fine if not everyone you meet automatically become friends. 

On the other hand, there are genuinely interesting people that are nice to have conversation wise and I do extend and offer to hang out again or talk another time. Not everyone takes up on that offer and I do respect it. Most people don’t respond to that question so I assume the solid answer is a no. Though more often than not, it would be the “Yeah see you soon!”. It leaves room to eventually see each other again when our own schedules line up, and I’m cool with that.

Though it’s very interesting to see the people you were interested in seeing again don’t show up as much as the people you did not expect to see again do show up. I believe I’ve had more meetings with acquaintances lately than most of the regulars. That just how it tends to go when you grow to not have much of a preference in who you see as much considering most of the time I’ve been asked by name is to actually solve a tech related problem, listen in to some favor, or the “Oh I know a guy who uses Face Tracking come here come here!” (And yeah I’m genuinely entertained people like to call me over to demo product, I am a tech enthusiast after all).

Therein lies the million dollar question to ask myself… 

[What is My Identity, Exactly? Why is it that way? How do you operate as a person?] 

I’ve spent a fair share in solitude the last couple of months just to only think about my own voice, and nothing more. 

The one identity I could throw out right off the gate is a stoic. And from the outside in a professional setting I usually do not show my emotions at work and just get the job done. It would make that particular action a stoic. I know internally I can express my feelings a lot. The issue would be who. Without a main person to confide in, I feel that me writing these entries is the best way I can express myself without any remorse or guilt.

What I do know is that I’m a Wanderer on a good day, and any other day a Drifter. 
For those who are working towards getting to know me more? I start out as a blank canvas but as you leave your mark, there will definitely be different parts of me that will be revealed depending on if you ask any questions about me or if the environment is a good place to talk about myself. 

Those that do not ask anything about me, well I actually will say nothing about myself.

What makes me a Wanderer? I’m curious enough to want to see all sorts of people on my own. What kind of people are out there. Listen to people talk just about anything. More often than not, I do learn through context clues what kind of lives they live, their hardships, as well as But at the same time with how I usually drift from place to place online and only focus on just me existing and nothing more… I’m aware it will result me in not making long term friendship or the like. 

That’s where I feel I provide something unique to the table.

Long as you’re willing to talk, I offer unconditional acquaintanceship. I’ll join in and match the similar vibe the room has to give. 
I can also offer more than that but I leave it up to the individual to personally seek that out. 

What makes me a Drifter? Ah that’s the easier question to answer (but I realized I did not really explain this part in any of my previous Crit blogs). I treat all social interactions like it is iron man mode. A rogue lite. While in a previous entry over a year ago has explained how I interact with people in detail, I can summarize it for 2026.

This is how I operate as a Drifter: 

Unless the other person specifically wants to seek me out and talk to me again, then otherwise I will assume those individuals are not interested in keeping touch with me long term. I used to reach out to people and initiated conversations for the last decade. While I certainly learned more about how to socialize with people, it did hurt to know a fundamental truth is not everyone you meet will want to have you in their life in general.

I believe the duality of living as a Wanderer and a Drifter alongside being rejected a lot in many ways… It has resulted me in the losing that spark to initiate conversations with people much more often. Worse off…

I’ve lost…

[Losing The Familiar Feeling of the Warmth attached to a “Friend”] 

Perhaps it is part my own doing because of how many people I end up meeting online. 
Or… I am just very self aware after many long hours of being by myself reflecting back on my thoughts thus far. 

This is it, for those that have been reading for the long haul. This is the dreaded word right there that has plagued me for a couple years now. 

From my observation, this seems mostly true but I know the top three reasons why people would reach out to me privately are:

A) To ask for a favor
B) To need help with tech related issues 
C) To share a link or image 

After that, we usually go our own way.

I’ll admit, I’m so used to any of the above three and it was all demonstrated through other peoples’ actions that Well… My body just… Kind of adapted and my mind and body said, 

“Providing knowledge is mostly my purpose with just about everyone I met so… Maybe I’m not made to make friends with anyone.”

I’m sorry if the last sentence I wrote made you tear up or cry. Take your time if that’s the case… I can’t really cry about it because I’m honestly past that point so I’ll continue to explain.

You see, it is not the ability to socialize long enough to make connections to extend a friendship that is the problem. I just can't generate that feeling on my own. It would have to come from the other person who specifically calls me out and wants me to be their friend is my only saving grace and my main way to identify who is a friend to me. I 'used' to be able to have this feeling and can enact on that at least a decade ago. The best I can do is offer people if they wish to see me again they can reach out to me and leave it at that. And for most of you on a technicality, you may call this a friend right here.

My mind logically can't quantify that no matter how you spin it. After experiencing and meeting a fair share of people, the ones that I can feel a friend is brewing is specifically all the previous interactions with that specific *warmth* in the way they intend to approach me and want to be there for me without even saying a word. Those are the people I'm more impressed with. The ones that can choose who they want into their lives. 

That begs the question... Why did I lose this ability to choose people into my life? And at a glance, it honestly makes me feel like I fundamentally lost a core function that is required for me to socialize with other people at a reasonable pace. 

I've also lost...

[Losing the Concept of Choosing Long Term with People]

It took me a while to figure this one out and I accepted that this is only time that will end up becoming my best retrospective. This is about a whole decade later and I have finally figured it out. 

So, with my core value in terms of what I believe in. My biggest core value is letting other people have autonomy to choose their own lives and have the right to be with who they want to be. 

AKA - I call it "Freedom". 

It's been a core value that I idolized, believed in, worshipped even. Anyone that can be genuinely be themselves without much pressure were people I ended up enjoying getting to know more. Even if some of those people have vastly different core values and beliefs. It's that they were able to communicate strongly in general without the need for filters. 

Little did I know that just like in Physics, every belief you do have objectively has positives and negatives. There is a sense of kinetic energy to stick to what you believe in and do not compromise yourself as a person. 

That is not to say in long term relationships, there is naturally a give and take with some level or degree of compromising. It shouldn't be to the cost of changing yourself entirely as a person just to cater to them... Because fundamentally, this is about two people's lives intertwined. 

I have that freedom to be myself and do as I please because I do not have any obligation to be with anyone. 

Because I followed that core value for just about my entire life, there was an unintended consequence to that core concept of "Freedom".

That consequence was dished out in the form of having an infinite loop of wandering around and meeting new people constantly to the point that I lost nearly all semblance of what it is like to be close to someone. Believe me when I've said, I've tried to even get closer to people in the process the last decade and it did not pan out all that well. Not because major mistakes were made, but from my perception: I just didn't really stand out enough towards other people to make them stay attracted for long. 

Yeah, that definitely hurts big time. I get it. But at least I did the best I can for them and just about everyone is still in talking terms. So I at least can feel relieved knowing that I did my best communicating. However, I can not say that in terms of reaching out to other people. There's two different ratings I'll give myself to that.

If it is in regard to respecting people's boundaries? I'd say I did just about a stellar job and the rare occasion or two it was crossed? I immediately owned up to it and let them know it won't happen again. 

If it is in regard to reaching out to people more often? It's a failing grade really. 

It's just... Throughout my entire life living, I was really only told or had conversations with only when I did something wrong or constructive criticism. I did not really get to have small talk or genuine conversations as much. When I looked around myself in a general public, I do see that people are having fun talking in the moment and I envied that sensation. And for the longest time, I really was terrible with making any conversation. When I was younger, I was the socially awkward person. I got made fun of a lot. 

It turns out that I haven't really found people I've clicked well with. Anime and online culture was not that strong at all outside of the Anime Club at my high school... So you definitely had strange looks if you told someone you like anime. And even then, that younger self was very smart as he had senses of knowing when he overstayed his welcome or knew he wasn't liked. So he ends up just walking away to avoid confrontation. If he couldn't avoid confrontation, he would just let them say whatever awful words at him and he'd just take it and then walk away after. 

I've went to talk to many friends who have had partners, observed how they interacted, then I get curious at times about how they first met, how they ended up falling in love and so on. Each person gave a different answer but the most common thread was that 'it just clicked' naturally. 

That only ends up with me being more concerned about myself and that devastating quote I told myself before in this entry... I'll bring it back again, right now:

“Providing knowledge is mostly my purpose with just about everyone I met so… Maybe I’m not made to make friends with anyone.”

It starts to make it feel like it extends more than just being friends at that point. This is probably the point where I ended up breaking down just about every quarter when I have a good first impression. Then things just fade away or fizzle out. Whether it is due to the passing of time or life just happens. 

Honestly, the best I can do is to control my reaction to those who are no longer present today...

* Act III - Facing the New Reality of Being Alone *

[How do I now live my life, knowing what I've experienced and written today?...]

The good news is for now, there's at least a work life balance of the normal 40 hours so I've had time to really iron this out, write this all down and put it out there.

I'll be extremely honest here: There is no morale to this story. There is no lessons learned. It's just that... I am living in my own life and I realize that not everyone has the happy ending they were looking for. So people will fight as hard as they can with their life to turn nothing into something tangible that is remotely positive into their life. 

I have told several of you the importance of a third space such as the Discord server you're reading this from. The average human is required to have this third space because as humans, we chase for that sense of relatability, to belong somewhere, to interact with people in a given community that is outside the closed circle of close friends, loved ones, and family. When those needs are all fulfilled, according to the account of many people they all tell me they're happy with who they have in their lives and enjoy it for what it is, despite the awful people they've met in the past. When that gets all cleared up, they do praise everyone positive that impacted them in their lives. It's a beautiful thing to hear... Very much so...

What happens when you come across a guy who just exists in a community, makes some random commentary or a funny joke here and there. Then get back to sitting down and continuing to exist. No more words mentioned. No exchanges. He just sits there on his own corner. He will definitely interact with you if you call him by name and will reciprocate the energy and topics of the conversations you give him. But when all is said and done, he goes back to staying silent and acknowledges that he had fun having a conversation with you. And leaves it at that. 

It's pretty much me in every single instance of a social space I've been in.

Of my entire time living my life, it has taught me one thing that's specific to myself: 

"The secret of happiness is this: let your interest be as wide as possible and let your reactions to the things and persons who interest you be as far as possible friendly rather than hostile." - Bertrand Russel 

However, with my current flaws on who I am as a person... This quote can only carry myself so far. I recognize that current quote is not enough. If life were that easy, then that quote would of satisfied me in whole. But unfortunately it did not... 

I needed more than just that quote...

I should also on top of that existing quote above, tell myself this:

"There are just going to be people out there who will have a strong first impression and you may click well with. However, it is a safe assumption to establish early on that nobody owes you their time. They have a life to live too! They have obligations to fulfill! They have a social circle of people they really like to be around that took months or years to develop! Committed relationships to be in! AND YOU'RE NOT ONE OF THOSE PEOPLE IF YOU JUST SHOWED UP OUT OF THE BLUE IN A PUBLIC SPACE!...

The world is large. The world is scary. I DON'T KNOW WHAT THE HELL I AM DOING TALKING TO PEOPLE ALL I DO IS YAP! If you don't know who is actually there for you and let alone... Lose the feeling of making new connections on your own? That's fine, people will go out of their way to find you. All you need to do is just exist in a public place. And definitely interact in that space when you find something that catches your attention. Just don't stay in one place for too long if nothing happens or you've been treated poorly. But if you lost all hope and energy, then just exist somewhere... " - Critical Hit, 9/26/2026 9:30 PM (CST)

I've come to the decision that the social flaws I have, are deep-seeded in nature and it is not going to be cured at all. Instead, I need to work around these flaws.

The best solution I got that appears to be working well for all of you, is that I simply live in the moment. Enjoy the moment for what it is. But I no longer hold the expectation of anyone to be close to me to save myself from disappointment, rejection, and to keep me level headed so I don't make grand illusions of assuming I feel close to anyone. But to instead trust the people who do interact with me are doing so in good terms and to continue with the good vibes. Definitely ask if anyone is attempting to get serious with me as well. As I've learned that situationships are a thing from a couple of people... Not a good thing to have from the sounds of it, but it exists...

There is a sense of liberation to know that in a third place, the only thing you're really responsible for is keeping the atmosphere chill and at peace to enable more conversations with people. And in the grand scheme of things, when more people are able to talk to each other freely with good intentions, that's where everyone in the respective community wins.

I can unfortunately not say the same for myself as I am way too self-aware of everything that goes around me. Knowing all the social cues I know now, it feels like I've read a guide on how social interaction works and I can't really unsee this anymore. 

It just... Really feels hard to enjoy being in social spaces now with all this knowledge burdened in my mind and having a very sharp awareness of how people's emotions and intents are in their mind but... 

Hey I'm going to keep trying anyway and just simply be...

Me.

title: Cloudformation - ECS wellcome-docker
content:
AWSTemplateFormatVersion: "2010-09-09"

Description: >
  Aplicacion Docker welcome-to-docker ejecutandose en ECS Fargate.

Parameters:
  VpcId:
    Type: AWS::EC2::VPC::Id
    Description: VPC donde se ejecutara la aplicacion

  PublicSubnetId:
    Type: AWS::EC2::Subnet::Id
    Description: Subred publica con salida a Internet

Resources:

  ECSCluster:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Cluster
    Properties:
      ClusterName: welcome-cluster

  TaskExecutionRole:
    Type: AWS::IAM::Role
    Properties:
      RoleName: !Sub "${AWS::StackName}-execution-role"
      AssumeRolePolicyDocument:
        Version: "2012-10-17"
        Statement:
          - Effect: Allow
            Principal:
              Service:
                - ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com
            Action:
              - sts:AssumeRole
      ManagedPolicyArns:
        - !Sub arn:${AWS::Partition}:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy

  WebSecurityGroup:
    Type: AWS::EC2::SecurityGroup
    Properties:
      GroupDescription: Permite acceder a la aplicacion web
      VpcId: !Ref VpcId
      SecurityGroupIngress:
        - Description: HTTP publico para la demo
          IpProtocol: tcp
          FromPort: 80
          ToPort: 80
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0
      SecurityGroupEgress:
        - IpProtocol: -1
          CidrIp: 0.0.0.0/0

  WelcomeTaskDefinition:
    Type: AWS::ECS::TaskDefinition
    Properties:
      Family: welcome-task
      RequiresCompatibilities:
        - FARGATE
      NetworkMode: awsvpc
      Cpu: "256"
      Memory: "512"
      ExecutionRoleArn: !GetAtt TaskExecutionRole.Arn
      ContainerDefinitions:
        - Name: welcome
          Image: docker/welcome-to-docker:latest
          Essential: true
          PortMappings:
            - ContainerPort: 80
              HostPort: 80
              Protocol: tcp

  WelcomeService:
    Type: AWS::ECS::Service
    Properties:
      ServiceName: welcome-service
      Cluster: !Ref ECSCluster
      LaunchType: FARGATE
      DesiredCount: 1
      TaskDefinition: !Ref WelcomeTaskDefinition
      NetworkConfiguration:
        AwsvpcConfiguration:
          AssignPublicIp: ENABLED
          Subnets:
            - !Ref PublicSubnetId
          SecurityGroups:
            - !Ref WebSecurityGroup

Outputs:

  ClusterName:
    Description: Nombre del cluster ECS
    Value: !Ref ECSCluster

  ServiceName:
    Description: Nombre del servicio ECS
    Value: !GetAtt WelcomeService.Name

  SecurityGroupId:
    Description: Security Group utilizado
    Value: !Ref WebSecurityGroup
